brand.name: Atlas Notes
brand.tagline: Geography, one story at a time

scenes.text: Four places that changed their names or their capitals in under a year.
In November twenty twenty-one, Barbados became a republic, fifty-five years after independence.
In January twenty twenty-two, Indonesia passed a law to move its capital from Jakarta to Nusantara, on Borneo.
In June, the United Nations began using the name Türkiye for Turkey, at the country's request.
And in September, Kazakhstan renamed its capital from Nur-Sultan back to Astana.

stories.headline: Barbados becomes a republic
stories.detail: A president replaced the British monarch as head of state on 30 November 2021.

stories.headline: Indonesia votes to move its capital
stories.detail: A January 2022 law names Nusantara, in East Kalimantan, as the successor to Jakarta.

stories.headline: The UN adopts the name Türkiye
stories.detail: The change followed a formal request from the government in Ankara in June 2022.

stories.headline: Nur-Sultan is Astana again
stories.detail: The capital took back the name it held from 1998 to 2019.
